rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from God's exalted perfection and human lowliness to divine precision, contrasting human crookedness with excellence granted by God.
rows.anchor: ولما ثبت ما لصفته تعالى من العلو , ولصفة الإنسان من السفول تلاه بما لأفعاله تعالى من الإتقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are signs of complete knowledge and power; both are needed to benefit from time, just as religious responsibility requires clear and ambiguous revelation.
rows.anchor: آية الليل كالآيات المتشابهة , وآية النهار كالمحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night's sign is erased by removing its light, so visible things cannot be seen, like writing made unreadable by erasure.
rows.anchor: بإعدام الضياء فجعلناها لا تبصر بها المرئيات كما لا يبصر الكتاب إذا محي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun makes daylight luminous; calling the day itself seeing is emphatic rhetoric because anyone with sight sees by it.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت في غاية الضياء يبصر بها كل من له بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternating light and darkness resembles human movement from deficiency to perfection and back, through haste prompted by nature and deliberation prompted by reason; the moon is also less than the sun.
rows.anchor: من انتقال من نقصان إلى كمال ومن كمال إلى نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day and night enable seeking God's bounty by day and benefiting from coolness at night; their movement also reveals the number of years without calculation.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليكم فيهما بضياء هذا تارة وبرد هذا أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The luminaries mark risings, settings, increase, decrease, and other events; their changes remain precise until the world's end, while without their difference times would merge and affairs cease.
rows.anchor: يدلان على حساب المطالع والمغارب , والزيادة والنقصان , وغير ذلك من الكوائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained everything else needed for religion or worldly life in detail, showing that nothing He wills is beyond His power.
rows.anchor: غيرهما مما تحتاجون إليه في دينكم أو دنياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every human is naturally restless, and the allotted bird is the person's predestined good or evil deed; the image reflects Arabs' use of omens before important actions.
rows.anchor: عمله الذي قدرناه عليه من خير وشر , ولعله عبر به لأنهم كانوا لا يقدمون ولا يحجمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deed is bound to a person's neck, a place of adornment or disgrace, and cannot be escaped, as one cannot escape one's neck.
rows.anchor: الذي محل الزين بالقلادة ونحوها , والشين بالغل ونحوه , إلزاما لا يقدر أن ينفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's imposed scripture and decree likewise could not be escaped; in the end only what was eternally decreed can appear.
rows.anchor: فلا يمكن أن يظهر في الأبد إلا ما قضى به في الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record contains every deed: recording angels write it daily and compare it with the Preserved Tablet, finding no discrepancy.
rows.anchor: تكتبه حفظتنا كل يوم , ثم إذا صعدوا قابلوا ما فيه على ما سطرناه قديما في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person reads the book personally rather than relying on another reader; God grants this ability whether the person is literate or not.
rows.anchor: أنت بنفسك غير ملزم بما يقرأه غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record has no additions or omissions; if the tongue denies an entry, the person's limbs testify against it.
rows.anchor: ولا ترى فيه زيادة ولا نقصا , ولا تقدر أن تنكر منه حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits its follower alone through a reward that does not pass to another; misguidance harms its follower alone through punishment.
rows.anchor: لأن عقابه عليه , لا يتجاوزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No burden-bearer takes another's sin; each receives recompense for their own action, so the guided are rewarded and the errant punished.
rows.anchor: لتخفيف عنها , بل لكل جزاء عمله لا تيعداه إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not punish before sending a messenger; whoever receives the call and disobeys arrogantly is punished, a rule fulfilled through Adam and later prophets.
rows.anchor: فمن بلغته دعوته فخالف أمره واستكبر عن اتباعه عذبناه بما يستحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls the command to inspect creation repeatedly, including the verse about sight returning humbled and weary.
rows.anchor: { ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers were sent to every community and no community lacked a warner, so their calls spread across the lands.
rows.anchor: فإن دعوتهم إلى الله تعالى قد انتشرت , وعمت الأقطار واشتهرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh claim that they had not heard this in the later religion implies they heard it in an earlier one; anyone reached by any prophetic call who neglects inquiry deserves punishment.
rows.anchor: فإنه يفهم أنهم سمعوه في الملة الأولى فمن بلغته دعوة أحد منهم بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the common claim that people of the interval are saved, citing prophetic reports that pre-Islamic ancestors are in Hell and that a dung beetle is better than them.
rows.anchor: مع إخبار النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم أن آباءهم الذين مضوا في الجاهلية في النار

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Hulaymi holds that a sane, discerning person who saw and reflected but adopted no religion is an unbeliever, since earlier prophets' numerous calls were likely to have reached him.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله الحليمي أحد أجلاء الشافعية وعظماء أئمة الإسلام رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Hulaymi argues that a call can reach people through opponents as well as followers; a capable thinker who hears a call to God but declines rational examination has turned away from it and disbelieved.
rows.anchor: فإن الخبر قد يبلغ علىلسان المخالف كما يبلغ على لسان الموافق

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Hulaymi allows that someone who truly never heard of religion, a prophet, or God might differ, though this seems unlikely; scholars disagree whether reason alone obligates faith or transmission is required.
rows.anchor: وإن أمكن أن يكون لم يسمع قط بدين ولا دعوة نبي ولا عرف نبي

rows.speaker: الزركشي عن الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi transmits al-Shafi'i's view that it is difficult for the prophetic call not to reach anyone, except perhaps people beyond the river in their region.
rows.anchor: قال الزركشي في آخر باب الديات من شرحه على المنهاج : وقد أشار الشافعي

rows.speaker: الدميري عن الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Dumayri also reports al-Shafi'i as saying that no one remains who has not received the call.
rows.anchor: وقال الدميري : وقال الشافعي : ولم يبق من لم تبلغه الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree to destroy a town does not remove its just claim to punishment; the matter follows intelligible norms by which people recognize wrongdoing and desert.
rows.anchor: قرر أسبابه وعرف أنها بقدره , وأن قدره لا يمنع حقوق العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills a town's destruction, He draws its affluent leaders into sin through abundant blessings and removal of hardship, which become an inducement to arrogance and disobedience.
rows.anchor: استدرجناهم بإدرار النعم ودفع النقم على ما يعلمون من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words about forgetting reminders refer to reminders delivered by messengers; once these were abandoned, blessings and opportunities were opened.
rows.anchor: { فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent are singled out because others follow them, and because privileged people owe the greatest gratitude and are most deserving of retribution for disbelief.
rows.anchor: وخص المترفين لأن غيرهم لهم تبع , ولأنهم أحق الناس بالشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation is that God commanded the affluent to obey but they disobeyed; God never commands indecency, and subordinates followed their leaders into shared sin and destruction.
rows.anchor: لأنا لا نأمر بالفحشاءن وقد جرت العادة بأن المترف عسر الانقياد

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Ya'qub reads آمرنا with a lengthened initial alif, meaning God made the community numerous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب : آمرنا - بمد الهمزة بمعنى كثرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root explanation links abundance to command, understood as the opposite of prohibition and an outcome of the power associated with numbers.
rows.anchor: والكثرة راجعة إلى الأمر الذي هو ضد النهي , فإنه نتيجة العز الذي هو لازم الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation derives the wording from consultation: God gave the affluent what they requested as a test, and they became arrogant and sinful.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من المؤامرة , أي أمرناهم بأوامرنا فما امتثلوا

rows.speaker: البخاري عن ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn Mas'ud's report that in pre-Islamic Arabia people said a clan had become آمر when it grew numerous.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : كنا نقول للحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning became due after messengers removed excuses: some actively sinned while others remained silent, a pattern deserving punishment by ordinary social standards.
rows.anchor: بمباشرة البعض للفسق وسكوت الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the town in sudden, thorough devastation, making it like crumbled clay; despite divine greatness, its destruction was effortless.
rows.anchor: أي أهلكناها إهلاكا شديدا بغتة غير مبالين بها فجعلناها كالمدرة المفتتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith cited to explain the root says the best wealth includes a productive mare and an abundantly foaling one.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث ( خير المال سكة مأبورة ومهرة مأمورة ) أي كثيرة النتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visible examples of destroyed towns make the warning more forceful to the heart and frightening to the soul.
rows.anchor: لأن الاعتبار بالمشاهد أوقع في القلب وأهول عند النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not seize those towns without warning: He sent messengers and gave them time until the decreed time arrived and their sins warranted punishment.
rows.anchor: ولم نستعجل في إهلاك قرية منهم ولا أخذناهم من غير إنذار , بل أرسلنا فيهم وأملينا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many nations after Noah were destroyed only after time and warning; Noah's people had been the earth's inhabitants, and their destruction carried monotheism's message to all later people.
rows.anchor: أمهلناهم حتى أعذرنا إليهم ثم أخذناهم في مدد متفاوتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording of the Torah and the Qur'an's silence, as many exegetes read it, indicate that people before Noah were not unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأما من قبل نوح فالظاهر من عبارة التوراة وسكوت القرآن أنهم لم يكونوا كفارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many exegetes make this point when interpreting the statement that people were one community.
rows.anchor: صرح كثير من المفسرين في تفسير ^ ( { كان الناس أمة واحدة } ) ^ [ البقرة : 213 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows servants' sins from eternity, including what is hidden, while humans cannot judge true character; apparent piety may change under testing or conceal grave private sins.
rows.anchor: فهو يعلم السر وأخفى , وأما أنتم فلستم هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may appear among the greatest righteous, yet testing can reveal that their final state is deeply misguided.
rows.anchor: فكم من إنسان كنتم ترونه من أكابر الصالحين ثم أسفرت عاقبته عند الامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God treats people according to His knowledge of their inner good and evil; attachment to leadership, wealth, and pleasure can prevent obedience to messengers.
rows.anchor: يعاملهم على حسب علمه على وجه معرف بعلمه بجميع طوياتهم من خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person seeking only the immediate world receives some, not all, of what God wills for selected people; the outcome depends on divine power rather than the seeker's strength.
rows.anchor: مما يريده لا جميع ما يريده ؛ ثم أبدل من ( له ) قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants worldly benefit only to those He wills, showing the outcome depends on Him rather than everyone who seeks it.
rows.anchor: أي لا لكل من أراد ذلك , تنبيها على أن ذلك بقوتنا لا بقوة ذلك المريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly-only seeker ultimately enters Hell disgraced and driven away; denial brings loss in both lives, while partial worldly success still leaves unmet wishes and afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: أي مفعولا به الذم , وهو ضد المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If denied worldly wishes the seeker suffers both losses; if granted something, the person still fails to receive everything desired and faces next-life punishment.
rows.anchor: فقل الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة , وإن أعطى فهو لا يعطي كل ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the afterlife must be joined to its proper effort: actions pleasing to God as prescribed in the Book and Sunna, not unsupported practices; intention needs action, actually when possible and by capacity when not.
rows.anchor: وهو ما كانت جديرة به من العمل بما يرضي الله بما شرعه في كتابه وسنة رسوله

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say work is useless without established faith, sincere intention, and correct action; the author identifies this firmness with the surah's ideal of excellence.
rows.anchor: من لم يكن له ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله : إيمان ثابت , ونية صادقة , وعمل مصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife seeker must be a steadfast believer; only then is the effort accepted and repaid with multiplied reward.
rows.anchor: أي مقبولا مثابا عليه بالتضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth may be given to David and Solomon for God's favored work or withheld from another as an honor, never as humiliation; status before God depends on deeds.
rows.anchor: مع أن بعضهم نفتح عليه الأبواب الدنيا كداود وسليمان عليهما الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether worldly provision is present or absent, it neither honors nor disgraces its recipient; real status before God comes from deeds.
rows.anchor: فالحاصل أنها إن وجدت عند الوالي لم تشرفهن وإن عدمت عنه لم تحقره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives both worldly seekers and afterlife seekers from His bounty; restriction can protect believers from a fleeting world, while abundance can provide a field for obedient service.
rows.anchor: أي من الفريقين : مريد الدنيا ومريد الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's worldly gift is not withheld from believer or unbeliever and includes immeasurable wealth, metals, gems, fruits, and provisions people could not continually collect.
rows.anchor: أي ممنوعا في الدنيا عن مؤمن ولا كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly provision is abundant beyond human accounting, including metals, jewels, fruits, and food for people and animals.
rows.anchor: بل هو ملء السهل والجبل من الذهب والفضة والحديد والنحاس والجواهر والثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly differences make some serve others, although God's created provision is equally available; only a powerful ruler imposes this hierarchy, so desire belongs toward Him.
rows.anchor: فصار الفاضل يسخر المفضول , والمفضول يرغب في خدمة المفضل ويتشف بالتقرب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife distinctions are greater than worldly ones, both in Paradise and Hell themselves and in their respective levels.
rows.anchor: أولا بالجنة والنار أنفسهما , وثانيا بالدرجات في لاجنة والدركات في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests that increased worldly provision often means a reduced afterlife share through sin or neglect, and points to God's differing degrees among prophets as a reason to seek lasting eminence.
rows.anchor: ولعل في ذلك إشارة إلى أن أكثر من يزاد في الدنيا تكون زيادته نقصا من آخرته بسبب ذنب اكتسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with noble character and high aspiration should prefer lasting elevation in the afterlife over worldly rank.
rows.anchor: فقال تعالى : { ولقد فضلنا بعض , النبيين على بعض } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone has all command and perfection, no other deity exists; addressing the Prophet first makes the warning more compelling to followers, though it may address everyone.
rows.anchor: يخاطب الرأس لأن ذلك أوقع في أنفس الأتباع , وإشارة إلى أنه لا يوحده حق توحيده سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating another deity leaves a person blamed and unsupported in this life, with no one able to secure help through intercession or otherwise.
rows.anchor: أي غير منصور فيما أردته من غير أن يغني عنك أحد بشفاعة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb translated decreed means both forbade associating partners and firmly commanded worship of God alone; all people in the Prophet's community are addressed.
rows.anchor: أي نهاك عن ذلك وأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding recognition of the sole benefactor, the passage commands kindness to parents as the first human nurturers; follow them in truth, reject their falsehood, and treat them gently unless that causes corruption.
rows.anchor: بالإتباع في الحق إن كانا حنيفين شاكرين لأنعمه كإبراهيم ونوح عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding ma to the conditional particle intensifies the instruction because of the importance of parents; reaching old age means they need the child as their only caretaker.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا بإدخال ( ما ) على الشرطية لزيادة التقرير للمعنى اهتماما بشأن الأبوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff forbids displaying annoyance toward parents; the reference to al-Ahqaf is useful for understanding this command.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتضجر منهما , وفي سورة الأحقاف ما ينفع كثيرا هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rebuking parents means scolding them harshly, with shouting and severity, and is explicitly prohibited.
rows.anchor: فيما لا ترضاه ؛ والنهرك زجر بإغلاظ وصياح

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali rejects the jurists' claim that uff is the least disobedience: it is among the worst because it is said of something repulsive, so the following prohibition on rebuking is neither an equal nor a fortiori case.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي رحمه الله في كتابه في أصول الفقه : وقد أولع الأصوليون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noble speech replaces rebuke and shows pleasing gentleness, tenderness, compassion, comfort, and emotional ease, with affectionate words such as father and mother.
rows.anchor: أي حسنا جميلا يرضاه الله ورسوله مع ما يظهر فيه من اللين والرقة والشفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing of humility evokes a bird lowering its wing; the child should show mercy from genuine compassion, not merely command or past obligation.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الطائر يخفض جناحه عند الذل , استعار لتعطفه عليهما رعيا لحقوقهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God for lasting mercy for the parents in return for their finite mercy and care in raising the child when helpless.
rows.anchor: بكرمك برحمتك الباقية وجودك كما برحمتهما أنا برحمتي القاصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for parents applies only to Muslims, according to the verse forbidding the Prophet to seek forgiveness for polytheists; it is not abrogated.
rows.anchor: وهذا مخصوص بالمسلمين بآية { ما كان للنبي } لا منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage pairs kindness to parents with monotheism and ends in prayer for their salvation, forbidding even slight contempt despite the strain of caregiving.
rows.anchor: حيث بدأه بأن شفع الإحسان إليهما بتوحيده ونظمه في سلكه , وختمه بالتضرع في نجاتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether a child truly intends kindness or only pretends; goodness requires disciplining oneself to treat parents as a cause of divine mercy.
rows.anchor: أي منكم { بما في نفوسكم } من قصد البر بهما وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteousness is conduct aligned with evidence, whether piety or excellence; those who repeatedly return to good after lapses are forgiven when they repent.
rows.anchor: والصلاح : استقامة الفعل على ما يدعوا إليعه الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands or constricts provision to train servants according to what benefits them, not to dishonor the restricted or honor the recipient; believers should follow His balanced example in spending.
rows.anchor: بأن ذلك إنما هو لتربية العباد بما يصلحهم , لا لهوان بالمضيق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows with complete insight which expansion or restriction benefits or harms each servant.
rows.anchor: بما يكون من كل القبض والبسط لهم مصلحة أو مفسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses people who killed daughters from fear of future poverty; calling them children evokes tenderness and signals the Prophet was free from this custom before and after Islam.
rows.anchor: معبرا بلفظ الولد هو داعية إلى الحنو والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children are named before their parents because poverty is feared from future support, unlike the other passage where poverty already exists and parents are named first as recipients of provision.
rows.anchor: مقدما ضمير الأولاد لكون الإملاق مترقبا من الإنفاق عليهم غير حاصل في حال القتل

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes the readings of khata': with a still vowel it means deliberate deviation from what is right, while the vocalized form can mean unintended error.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : والخطأ - أي بكسر ثم سكون - لا يكون إلا تعمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach fornication even through preliminaries or by entertaining it; it can arise from need or desire, destroy lineage, produce wrongful life, and lead to strife and killing.
rows.anchor: أي أدنى قرب بفعل شيء من مقدماته ولو بإخطاره بالخاطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fornication is extremely indecent and forbidden alongside the condemnation of indecency; calling it a path indicates its wide, frequently used course.
rows.anchor: وقد نهاكم عن الفحشاء في آية العدل والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from withholding through miserliness, to reckless giving in fornication, to wrongful acquisition of what is lacking through transgression.
rows.anchor: فصارت الأسباب المنهي عنها بتحريم مسبباتها منع الموجود بخلا ثم بذله إسرافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A life is protected by Islam or covenant and may be taken only under a lawful right; the three stated cases are unbelief, adultery after marriage, and intentional wrongful killing of a believer.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعلى الذي له الأمر كله بالإسلام أو العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victim's relative or ruler receives authority to seek justice, but may not kill anyone besides the killer or exceed the due limit.
rows.anchor: أي سواء كان قريبا أو سلطانا { سلطانا } أي أمرا متسلطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The murdered person is supported by social revulsion against killing in this life and by full recovery of the right in the next; confidence in this support prevents retaliatory excess.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا بما جبل الله في الطباع من فحش القتلن وكراهة كل أحد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prohibiting attacks on life and sexual honor, the text protects property as their equivalent support, beginning with the vulnerable orphan whose wealth tempts others.
rows.anchor: أتبعه النهي عن نهب ما هو عديلها , لأن به قوامهان وهو الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach an orphan's property except through the best beneficial management that grows it, until the orphan reaches maturity and discernible sound judgment.
rows.anchor: من طرائق القربان , وهو التصرف فيه بالغبطة تثميرا لليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping a covenant covers the whole category of agreements and every time, place, and condition needed to fulfill their terms; a covenant is a contract made for assurance.
rows.anchor: أي بسببه ليتحقق الوفاء به ولا يحصل فيه نقص ما , وهو العقد الذي يقدم للتوثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is described as answerable because God knows whether it was kept or broken, as though it witnesses against the agent.
rows.anchor: أي كونا من يتأتى منه السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When measuring for others, give the full measure; weighing must use a just, upright balance without bias.
rows.anchor: أي نفسه فإنه أمر محسوس لا يقع فيه إلباس واشتباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fair dealing is better in both lives and has the best outcome; the comparative wording grants the opponent's premise for argument, though a rational person should not settle for less good.
rows.anchor: أي عاقبة في الدارين , وهو تفعيل من الأول وهو الرجوع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that righteousness settles the heart and soul, while sin unsettles the heart and chest even if legal authorities give a favorable ruling.
rows.anchor: ( البر ما سكن إليه القلب واطمأنت إليه النفس , والإثم ما حاك في القلب وتردد في الصدر وإن أفتاك المفتون وأفتوك )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم
rows.claim: A saying inherited from the earliest prophecy warns that one who feels no shame may do as desired.
rows.anchor: ( إن مما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى : إذا لم تستحي فاصنع ما شئت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not follow what one does not know, especially slander and accusation; require certainty where certainty is required and stop at reasonable probability where that is enough.
rows.anchor: أي تتبع أيها الإنسان مجتهدا بتتبع الآثار { ما ليس لك به علم } من ذلك وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and sight are routes of perception and the heart its instrument; each is questioned about strenuous truth-seeking and acting on truth once found.
rows.anchor: وهما طريقا الإدراك { والفؤاد } الذي هو آلة الإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative form أولئك can refer to rational or non-rational things, as illustrated by an unattributed Arabic poem about days and homes.
rows.anchor: وأولاء وجميع أسماء الإشارة يشار بها للعاقل وغيره كقوله : ذم المنازل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that inner whisperings are forgiven unless acted upon or spoken; the author distinguishes unchosen whisper and thought from accountable intention and resolve because the latter are voluntary.
rows.anchor: ( إن الله تجاوز لأمتي عما حدثت به أنفسهم ما لم تعمل به أو تكلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride blocks knowledge that leads to good and embodies ignorance that leads to evil.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الكبر والأنفة أعظم موقف عن العلم الداعي إلى كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marah is intense joy entailing vanity, arising from impulsive desire and human deficiencies; boasting would only suit someone who attained every aim, which no creature can do.
rows.anchor: وهو شدة الفرح التي يلزمها الخيلاء , لأن ذلك من رعونات النفس بطيش الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot cut across the earth or reach the mountains in height, so human limits give no grounds for pride.
rows.anchor: أي ولو بأدنى الوجوه { الأرض } أي تقطعها سيرا من مكانك إلى طرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited acts and neglected duties are bad in God's sight and treated as disliked through prohibition, blame, and punishment; a recipient of divine beneficence should respond with gratitude.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر البعيد من المكارم { كان } أي كونا غير مزايل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine noun سيئة is treated as masculine because it became a lexicalized noun like sin and wrongdoing rather than remaining an adjective.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت السيئة قد صارت في حكم الأسماء كالإثم والذنب وزال عنها حكم الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address may be directed specifically to the Prophet, since no one else can fulfill the instruction fully and followers attend more carefully when their leader is addressed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بهذا الإفراد النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These commands and prohibitions are unbreakable wisdom; none was abrogated in any religious law, and they were present in every community.
rows.anchor: من حكمه هذه الأشياء المشار إليها من الأوامر والنواهي أنها لم تقبل النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating another god is the greatest ignorance; another is implied by the claim of partnership, and shirk ends the list because it is the most disgraceful wrong.
rows.anchor: وكان الشرك أعظم جهل , أتبعه - ليكون النهي عنه بدءا وختاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final threat of blame and expulsion is harsher than the earlier blame and lack of support; God begins with a milder warning and guides servants gradually.
rows.anchor: فهذان الوصفان أشنع من وصفي الذم والخذلان في الآية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is the greatest ignorance because deity must be one in essence, without division, and in attribute, without a genus.
rows.anchor: لأن من الواضح أن الإله لا يكون إلا واحدا بالذات فلا ينقسم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that these eighteen verses were on Moses' tablets, beginning with the prohibition on another god; they correspond to ten Torah commandments and begin and end rejecting shirk.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن هذه الثماني عشرة آية كانت في ألواح موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism is the root and key of all wisdom; without it, wisdom and learning do not benefit even those who surpass philosophers, who remain far from God's religion.
rows.anchor: لأن التوحيد رأس كل حكمة وملاكها , ومن عدمه لم تنفعه حكمه وعلومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling angels God's daughters implies likeness in divinity, and worshipping them enacts that claim, compounding the ignorance of mere shirk.
rows.anchor: ادعاءهم أن الملائكة بنات الله ادعاء لأن له مناسبا ومجانسا في أخص الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke exposes the inconsistency of claiming that God chose sons for people but took the supposedly inferior daughters for Himself, though they reject daughters and even kill them.
rows.anchor: ثم التفت إليهم مخاطبا بما دل على تناهي الغضب فقال : { أفأصفاكم ربكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording first says sons because the term sounds pleasing, then females to suggest softness and daughters; it highlights that people reserve stronger male children for themselves while assigning weak female angels to God.
rows.anchor: وعبر أولا بالبنين دون الذكور لأن اسم الابن ألذ في السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim is grave falsehood and ignorance: it attributes bodily offspring to God and prefers themselves over Him, despite the angels' obedience.
rows.anchor: أي في الجهل والإفك , عليه وعلى ملائكة الذين لا يعصونه ما أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God varied Qur'anic proofs, lessons, examples, laws, promises, warnings, commands, prohibitions, and clear or ambiguous passages, turning from one illustration to another.
rows.anchor: أي طرقنا تطريقا عظيما بأنواع طرق البيان من العبر والحكم , والأمثال والأحكام

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains that تصريف means turning something from one direction to another, then by extension making it clear.
rows.anchor: والتصريف لغة : صرف الشيء من جهة إلى أخرى , ثم صار كناية عن التبيين - قاله أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminder calls forth what is already rooted in human nature and reason; the assimilated reading suggests a little reminder suffices because God is generous.
rows.anchor: أي نوعا من التذكير - بما أشار إليه الإدغام , فإنه سبحانه كريم يرضى باليسير

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read with a still dhal and a damma on kaf, indicating Qur'anic truths are rooted in nature and reason and can be recalled after distractions are removed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بإسكان الذال وضم الكاف إشارة إلى أن جميع ما في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite varied explanation, the audience grows more averse even to listening because it mistakes proofs for sophistry and clings to inherited customs made familiar over generations.
rows.anchor: عن السماع فضلا عن التذكير , لاعتقادهم أن ذلك ليس ببراهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If other gods existed, they would seek a path to the Lord of the Throne either to overpower Him as earthly kings do or to gain standing through favor with Him.
rows.anchor: ليقهروه ويزيلوا ملكه كما ترون من فعل ملوك الدنيا بعضهم مع بعض , أو ليتخذوا عنده يدا تقربهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Lord of the Throne evokes God's grandeur and identifies both those seeking and the one sought.
rows.anchor: وصرح بالعرش تصويرا لعظمته وتعيينا للمبتغي والمبتغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly transcendent above the polytheists' claims and exalted in perfect attributes; the bare verbal noun signals the reality of the act despite the intensive verb form.
rows.anchor: أي تنزه التنزه الأعظم عن كل شائبة نقص { وتعالى } أي علا أعظم العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and every being praise God; capable beings do so verbally, and all creation also does so through signs revealed by its existence, order, and finitude.
rows.anchor: وهذا تسبيح بلسان المقال ممن يصح منه , وبلسان الحال منه ومن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation's origination indicates an eternal, uncreated maker; its precision indicates a wise governor, and its passing away indicates a powerful, freely acting sovereign.
rows.anchor: من جهة حدوثها إلى صانع أحدثها قديم غير مصنوع , ومن جهة إتقانها إلى كونه مدبرا حكيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says people do not comprehend creation's praise, rather than that they cannot hear it, because they turn from reflection; ordinary people differ from elect who hear inanimate praise.
rows.anchor: دون ( تسمعون ) { تسبيحهم } لإعراضكم عن النظر

rows.speaker: البخاري عن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn Mas'ud's report that on a journey the Prophet put his hand in a small vessel and water flowed between his fingers; companions also heard food glorifying God as it was eaten.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال : كنا نعد الآيات بركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glorification of pebbles is well known; David's Psalms repeatedly exhort readers to reflect on the praise offered by creation.
rows.anchor: وتسبيح الحصى مشهور , وفي زبور داود عليه السلام تكرير كثير لهذه الآية وحث على تأملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 68 says the heavens, earth, seas, and all creatures moving in them praise God.
rows.anchor: تسبح له السماوات والأرض والبحار وكل ما يدب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 85 declares that no one compares with God or His works and all created nations come to bow and praise His name because He is great and performs wonders.
rows.anchor: فليس مثلك يا ربي وإلهي ولا مثل أعمالك , لأن جميع الأمم الذين خلقت يأتون ويسجدون أمامك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 88 praises God's strength over enemies, His ownership of heaven and earth, creation of land and sea, and the praise of Tabor and Hermon; justice and mercy establish His rule.
rows.anchor: لك السماوات ولك الأرض , أنت أسست الدنيا بكمالها , خلقت البر والبحر , تابور وحرمون باسمك يسبحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 95 calls the whole earth to sing a new song, worship in God's holy courts, and tremble before the God who rules the peoples justly.
rows.anchor: سبحوا الرب تسبيحا جديدا , الأرض كلها تسبح الرب , اسجدوا للرب في هياكل قدسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 97 says that the whole earth praises God and glorifies Him.
rows.anchor: ولله تسبح كل الأرض , مجدوا وهللوا وسبحوا الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 148 lists angels, sun, moon, stars, waters, animals, plants, and people as praising the Lord, who created them and set their enduring limits.
rows.anchor: سبحوا الرب من السماوات , سبحوه من العلى يا جميع ملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 150 commands praise in God's sanctuary and power, by trumpet and loud sounds, concluding that every breath praises the Lord.
rows.anchor: سبحوا الله في كل قديسيه , سبحوه في جلد قوته , سبحوه كمثل جبروته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because creation's praise is clear, people deserve punishment for failing to understand it through neglect of reflection; their safety is only God's forbearance and delayed judgment.
rows.anchor: فكانوا مستحقين للعقاب في عدم فهمه بعدم التأمل في المصنوعات حق التأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing and does not hasten punishment for turning away from reflection; He is abundantly forgiving, encouraging repentance.
rows.anchor: حيث لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على إعراضكم عن صرف الأفكار فيما أمركم بصرفها إليه
